page: Amazon Web Services m5n.12xlarge is a network-enhanced general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, delivering 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation is 192 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography flags, and bit-manipulation primitives. The instance includes no local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data, and features zero dedicated GPU accelerators.

The primary differentiator of the m5n line is network performance, delivering a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks position the instance within the middle tier for compute and memory throughput. Multi-core performance is solid, logging 40,654.51 in stress-ng and 11,104.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, though single-core execution reflects older microarchitecture performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 1259.0 and a lower-quartile stress-ng single-core rating. Memory throughput achieves 107.74 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 47.84 GB/sec in uncached writes. In application benchmarks, the instance registered 37.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 27.01 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency scales favorably for deployments that require heavy network bandwidth without migrating to dedicated compute-optimized or high-memory instance classes. Because local storage is absent, storage costs and I/O rely entirely on attached network-based storage volumes. Workloads best aligned with the hardware profile of the m5n.12xlarge include network-bound database clusters, distributed in-memory caching nodes, ETL pipelines, software compilation servers, and scalable web application backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance designed for network-intensive workloads, operating on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, it supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and 192 GB of DDR4 RAM. The instance lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on remote EBS volumes. Its primary distinction is a 50 Gbps baseline network capability. Benchmark evaluations position its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in the median tier, demonstrated by 40,654.51 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 37.73 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread throughput exhibits lower-tier benchmark results, the substantial network capacity and balanced memory allocation make the instance a solid platform for distributed caching, database backends, ETL data pipelines, and high-concurrency web services.
